The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ffdf93f60ad3ab23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is L0 > 4, depending only on the fixed cutoff, such that for every L ≥ L0 and s ∈ [0, 1], Equation (2.9) has a smooth axisymmetric solution u = u0 + v on Ω, where u0 = 1 + r−1, satisfying ur + 1 2u = 0 on S, u −→ 1 as r −→ ∞. (3.1) It is unique among smooth solutions with v ≥ 0 and v = O(r−1). One may take a constant M = 3, independent of s, L, such that 1 ≤ u0 ≤ u ≤ M. Uniformly in these parameters, |v| + r|vr| ≤ Cs2 L−2 (r ≥ 1), |vrr| ≤ Cs2 L−2 (1 ≤ r ≤ 2). (3.2) For every integer k ≥ 0, all Cartesian derivatives satisfy |Dk v| ≤ Ck s2 L r−1−k , |Dk (u − 1)| ≤ Ckr−1−k . (3.3) For fixed L, s 7→ vs is continuous in the sup norm, as are s 7−→ Z R3 Hs dx, s 7−→ Ns(0) = 1 4π Z R3 Hs(x) |x| dx, where Hs = pu−7 s +ℓu−3 s is extended by zero inside the unit ball and Ns is its Newton potential. Moreover, 0 ≤ Z R3 Hs dx ≤ C s2 L , 0 ≤ Ns(0) ≤ C s2 L2 . (3.4) At s = 0 the solution is exactly u0.
